1.48.7.en: c. Tearing down the altars, breaking the pillars, cutting down the groves and burning the images with fire (Deut 7:5) means cleansing the heart (the temple of the Lord) from setting up other gods, such as self-love, the love of praise, or the satisfaction of the lusts of the flesh.

1.48.8.en: d. "Thine eye shall have no pity upon them" (Deut 7:6). Let the word of God be like a two-edged sword (Heb 4:12), separating truth from falsehood with power and discernment, without softness.

1.48.9.en: e. "Thou shalt not be afraid of them" (Deut 7:18). The spiritual man has authority (Deut 11:8); he does not fear sin nor dread the enemy of good, trusting in God who gives the victory (1 Cor 15:57).

1.48.10.en: In our study of the writings of St. John Cassian we saw that Origen holds that the principal sins in man's life are eight, and St. Evagrius took the same idea from him, and it spread in the writings of the Eastern and Western Fathers. The people of God overcame Pharaoh and his army, that is, the Egyptians, and here they overcome the seven nations mentioned here, as though God grants His Church the spirit of victory over the eight principal sins.

1.49.0.en: And the Arvadite, and the Zemarite, and the Hamathite. [16]

1.49.1.en: Arvadite: its meaning is wandering; it is now called Ruad, and lies on a small island about two miles from the Syrian shore and thirty miles north of Tripoli.

1.49.2.en: The Zemarite: a Canaanite tribe (Gen 10:18), who dwelt in Zemar or Zemara, the present Sumra on the coast between Arvad and Tripoli.

1.49.3.en: The Hamathite: he is the same as the one mentioned by the name Hamathite (Gen 10:18). He is the one who dwells in Hamath.

1.50.0.en: The sons of Shem; Elam, and Asshur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram, and Uz, and Hul, and Gether, and Meshech. [17]

1.50.1.en: Aram: its meaning is "exalted or lofty," and it occurs often in the Holy Bible; among them one of the five sons of Shem the son of Noah (Gen 10:22-23; 1 Chr 1:17); one of the sons of Kemuel the son of Nahor, Abraham's brother (Gen 22:21); one of the sons of Shamer of the descendants of Asher (1 Chr 7:34); and the father of Amminadab and son of Hezron the son of Perez the son of Judah. It is the Greek form of the Hebrew name "Ram."

1.50.2.en: Uz: the homeland of Job, perhaps in the land of Edom.

1.50.3.en: Hul: an Aramaic name meaning "circle or revolution" (Gen 10:23). It is the Huliya mentioned by Ashurnasirpal in connection with Mount Masius.

1.51.0.en: And Arphaxad begat Shelah, and Shelah begat Eber. [18]

1.51.1.en: Arphaxad: its meaning is "the fortress of the Chaldeans." He was the grandfather of Eber, from whom some think the Hebrews take their name. He was the first to be born after the Flood by two years. He died at the age of four hundred and thirty-eight years (Gen 11:10-13).

1.51.2.en: Moses was careful to mention the sons of Arphaxad (Gen 10:24), for he begot Shelah, and Shelah begot Eber, and Eber begot Peleg, and Peleg Reu, and Reu Serug, and Serug Nahor, and Nahor Terah, who begot Abram, who married Sarai. Thus he began with the first starting point of the people with the appearance of Abram (Abraham), the father of the fathers. The prophet Moses also made clear Lot's kinship to Abraham, as the son of his brother Haran, the son of Terah.

1.51.3.en: Shelah: a Semitic name meaning "sprout or shoot."

1.51.4.en: Eber: a Hebrew name meaning "crossing over"; Abraham was the seventh of his descendants, and to him the Hebrews are attributed. He was also the ancestor of the Arabs and the Arameans (Gen 10:21, 25; 11:14-17).

1.52.0.en: And unto Eber were born two sons: the name of the one was Peleg; because in his days the earth was divided:

1.52.1.en: and his brother's name was Joktan. [19]

1.52.2.en: Eber and his son Peleg: St. Jerome sees that Eber, from whose offspring the Hebrews came, delivered a prophecy by naming his son "Peleg," which means "division," because in his days the language was divided at Babel. Men spoke one language, and when they thought of building a tower in defiance of God, who had allowed the flood in the days of Noah, their tongues were confused, and each nation in the region had its own language and culture. And God turned the discipline into the building up of the world and its progress.

1.52.3.en: It is told in (Gen 11:1-9) how the tongues of the Chaldeans were confused, who in their obstinacy toward God thought they were able to build a tower whose top would be in heaven, so that God could not discipline them with a flood again.

1.52.4.en: St. Mar Jacob of Serugh spoke of the blessings that mankind enjoyed at that time, as in all generations, through this discipline. For the people spread out into many regions, and with the multiplicity of languages there appeared a multiplicity of cultures for the building up of mankind, and it also relieved those working on the building of the tower from carrying exhausting burdens to build a tower that was of no use.

1.52.5.en: Joktan: a Semitic name meaning "he will be small," a person who became a tribe of the descendants of Shem, from which thirteen Arab tribes branched (Gen 10:25-30).

1.53.0.en: And Joktan begat Almodad, and Sheleph, and Hazarmaveth, and Jerah, [20]

1.53.1.en: Almodad: its meaning is "the beloved" or "beloved of God"; it refers to an Arab tribe in the south.

1.53.2.en: Sheleph: a Semitic name, perhaps meaning "one who plows the earth." He was of the Semitic people descended from Joktan, and dwelt in the south of the Arabian peninsula. This name is still famous in the land of Yemen.

1.53.3.en: Hazarmaveth: a Hebrew name meaning "village of death." It is the name of a region in the south of the Arabian peninsula that still bears the same name; its climate is unhealthy, and therefore it was called Hazarmaveth.

1.54.0.en: Hadoram also, and Uzal, and Diklah, [21]

1.54.1.en: Hadoram: the son of Joktan (Gen 10:26-27); to him is attributed one of the tribes that dwelt in the Arabian peninsula.

1.54.2.en: Uzal: he is Qahtan, who is considered the ancestor of the Arabs. Perhaps Uzal as the name of a place is the one mentioned in (Ezek 27:19) [the Septuagint].

1.54.3.en: Diklah: a Semitic name, perhaps meaning "palm tree." It was the name of a people descended from Joktan (Gen 10:27), who most probably dwelt in the Arabian peninsula.

1.55.0.en: And Ebal, and Abimael, and Sheba, [22]

1.55.1.en: Ebal: the son of Joktan, of the descendants of Eber, also called Obal (Gen 10:28). To him his descendants are attributed, and they are among the oldest tribes in the Arabian peninsula, especially in Yemen.

1.55.2.en: Abimael: its meaning is "my father is El," or "my father is God," or "God is my father." It denotes an Arab tribe whose homeland is the south of the Arabian peninsula.

1.56.0.en: And Ophir, and Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan. [23]

1.56.1.en: Ophir: it seems that he settled in the south of the land of the Arabs, because his name occurs with the names of Sheba and Havilah (Gen 10:29).

1.56.2.en: Jobab: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "a cry." It is not known where this Arab tribe dwelt.

1.57.0.en: 24 Shem, Arphaxad, Shelah, 25 Eber, Peleg, Reu, 26 Serug, Nahor, Terah, 27 Abram; the same is Abraham. 28 The sons of Abraham; Isaac, and Ishmael.

1.59.1.en: Serug: a Semitic name meaning "shoots or a branch." A city of this name was found near Haran.

1.59.2.en: Nahor: a Semitic name meaning "snorting" (breathing heavily), one of the descendants of Shem the son of Noah, the father of Terah and the grandfather of Abraham. He lived a hundred and forty-eight years (Gen 11:22-25).

1.59.3.en: Terah: a Hebrew name meaning "wild goat." He dwelt in Ur of the Chaldees, and worshipped idols (Josh 24:2), especially the moon. He accompanied Abraham on his journey to Haran in Mesopotamia, and died there (Gen 11:31-32).

1.60.1.en: Abraham (Abram): Abram was called Abraham by God, and the meaning is "father of a multitude" (Gen 17:5). His birthplace was Ur of the Chaldees. Its site now is Tell el-Muqayyar, nine miles from Nasiriyah on the River Euphrates in southern Iraq. He journeyed with his family and his father Terah a distance of 600 miles to the northwest of Jerusalem, and they settled in Haran on the Balikh, one of the tributaries of the Euphrates (Gen 11:26-32).

1.60.2.en: The Holy Bible gave attention to the story of Abraham, for he was unique in his faith in God, so he was made worthy to enjoy the divine promise and to become a blessing to many nations (Gen 11-25). He is mentioned in the New Testament more than seventy times.

1.60.3.en: The Lord Christ called the Kingdom of God "Abraham's bosom," when He says: "And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom" (Lk 16:22).

1.60.4.en: Many of the Fathers of the Church call the people of God "the daughter of Abraham," and they call St. Mary by the same title, and they reckon the believers sons of Abraham.

1.61.0.en: v Abraham (Gen 12-25) perceived in the Spirit that the birth of the Son was still far off, but he rejoiced to see His day in the Spirit without seeing it in the flesh (Jn 56:8)[52].

1.61.1.en: St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian v Our Lord, the Light, showed Himself in the darkness, and the night that had darkened the whole world fled.

1.61.2.en: He came down from the Father, and shone forth from the Virgin, the daughter of Abraham, and began to walk on the path He had paved in the world.

1.62.0.en: The Light had dwelt in the womb of the Virgin in holiness, and from there began His way in the flesh[53].

1.63.0.en: v Through Lazarus, who was reclining at Abraham's side, He gave courage to those whom poverty had bowed down (Lk 16:19-31)[54].

1.63.1.en: St. Mar Jacob of Serugh As he explains the parable of the laborers whom the owner of the vineyard hired (Mt 20:1-16), Serugh speaks of the house of Abraham in the procession of the righteous laborers.

1.63.2.en: The laborers of the third hour are the house of Noah.

1.63.3.en: And the laborers of the sixth hour are the house of Abraham.

1.63.4.en: And the laborers of the ninth hour are Moses and the prophets. The vineyard is the way of righteousness.

1.63.5.en: And the laborers of the eleventh hour are the peoples who were idle from the work of righteousness, whom the owner of the vineyard brought in to work in it at the end of the ages. The Jewish community, which had the prophets, the commandments and the laws, did not enter to work in the vineyard, so the peoples enter in its stead.

1.63.6.en: v If you consider: these workers of the third hour are the house of Noah, whom He set over His work.

1.63.7.en: The (laborers) of the sixth hour are the house of Abraham in the land of Aram, who girded themselves and put on righteousness like the former ones (Gen 12:4-5; Gen 22; Judg 19:10)(**).

1.63.8.en: These laborers of the ninth hour are the great Moses and Joshua the son of Nun and the whole choir of prophecy.

1.63.9.en: All the laborers of the house of God entered, and were completed in the vineyard of the Lord, which is the way of righteousness.

1.63.10.en: And the way of the righteous continued from Adam, and reached Noah, and reached Abraham and drew near to him.

1.63.11.en: And it passed on and the way reached the great Moses (the laborer of the) ninth hour, for he kept it much by the commandments of righteousness.

1.63.12.en: And the laborers toiled with zeal in the vineyard of the Beloved, those whom He hired and brought in four times (Isa 5:1).

1.63.13.en: And all of them strove, working righteousness: (Gen 4:26) the house of Seth and Enosh from the beginning of the great world.

1.63.14.en: And the house of Noah was added and lived in righteousness, and Abraham and Isaac arose, who worked with zeal.

1.63.15.en: And Moses came and with him the divine prophets, and they became good laborers in the vineyard, and were zealous in it.

1.63.16.en: And they arose like the wise, and put on the love of the new life, and toiled well in the vineyard of spiritual fruits...

1.63.17.en: The owner of the vineyard opened his door to the peoples of the earth, and all creation entered and worked for God.

1.63.18.en: At the end of the world, at the last of the times and seasons, all the peoples entered in the eleventh (hour) into the great house. And they began the way of righteousness with zeal, and wove and spun righteousness bodily[55].

1.63.19.en: St. Mar Jacob of Serugh v We must interpret the whole story of Abraham symbolically, and make everything spiritual, beginning with the commandment: "Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee" (Gen 12:1). This commandment was given not to Abraham alone, but to everyone who wishes to be his son[56].

1.64.0.en: The sons of Abraham; Isaac, and Ishmael. [28]

1.64.1.en: Isaac: the root is derived in the Semitic languages from the word "to laugh or to jest or to dance or to play." He was reckoned the son of the promise; his father was a hundred years old and his mother ninety when he was born. And he was reckoned the firstborn son in spite of his birth after Ishmael, whom Hagar, the servant of Abraham and Sarah, bore.

1.64.2.en: His marriage to Rebekah came as a type of the wedding between the Lord Christ and the Church, His spiritual bride.

1.64.3.en: v Isaac (Gen 21-28) also arose and was brought up in beauty, and trained himself in divine thoughts.

1.64.4.en: He filled his soul with faith and humility, and was armed with righteousness and uprightness.

1.64.5.en: And he hated strife, and lost his possessions without anger, and loved peace, and was calm and virtuous in his deeds[57].

1.64.6.en: St. Mar Jacob of Serugh v Isaac longed to see Him, because he tasted the flavor of His salvation (Heb 19:11)[58].

1.64.7.en: St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian Ishmael: his name means "God hears"; the son of Abraham by his Egyptian maidservant Hagar, whom he begot by the request of his wife Sarah. This was customary for one who was barren, and the son was attributed to the wife (Gen 16:2). However, Hagar despised her mistress, and in a kind of jesting Ishmael tried to kill Isaac (Gen 21:9; Gal 4:29).

1.65.0.en: 29 These are their generations: The firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth; then Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam, 30 Mishma, and Dumah, Massa, Hadad, and Tema, 31 Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These are the sons of Ishmael. 32 Now the sons of Keturah, Abraham's concubine: she bare Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah. And the sons of Jokshan; Sheba, and Dedan. 33 And the sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher, and Henoch, and Abida, and Eldaah. All these are the sons of Keturah. 34 And Abraham begat Isaac. The sons of Isaac; Esau and Israel. 35 The sons of Esau; Eliphaz, Reuel, and Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah. 36 The sons of Eliphaz; Teman, and Omar, Zephi, and Gatam, Kenaz, and Timna, and Amalek. 37 The sons of Reuel; Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. 38 And the sons of Seir; Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah, and Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan. 39 And the sons of Lotan; Hori, and Homam: and Timna was Lotan's sister. 40 The sons of Shobal; Alian, and Manahath, and Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. And the sons of Zibeon; Aiah, and Anah. 41 The sons of Anah; Dishon. And the sons of Dishon; Amram, and Eshban, and Ithran, and Cheran. 42 The sons of Ezer; Bilhan, and Zavan, and Jakan. The sons of Dishan; Uz, and Aran. 43 Now these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the children of Israel; Bela the son of Beor: and the name of his city was Dinhabah. 44 And when Bela was dead, Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his stead. 45 And when Jobab was dead, Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his stead. 46 And when Husham was dead, Hadad the son of Bedad, which smote Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Avith. 47 And when Hadad was dead, Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his stead. 48 And when Samlah was dead, Shaul of Rehoboth by the river reigned in his stead. 49 And when Shaul was dead, Baal-hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his stead. 50 And when Baal-hanan was dead, Hadad reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Pai; and his wife's name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab. 51 Hadad died also. And the dukes of Edom were; duke Timnah, duke Aliah, duke Jetheth, 52 Duke Aholibamah, duke Elah, duke Pinon, 53 Duke Kenaz, duke Teman, duke Mibzar, 54 Duke Magdiel, duke Iram. These are the dukes of Edom.

1.66.0.en: 29 These are their generations: The firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth; then Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam, 30 Mishma, and Dumah, Massa, Hadad, and Tema, 31 Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These are the sons of Ishmael.

1.66.2.en: The firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth; then Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam, [29]

1.66.3.en: He spoke of the genealogies of Ishmael as the son of the bondwoman, whose descendants may not inherit with the sons of the promise. They signify the unbelieving Jews who became rejected (Gal 4:22 ff.).

1.66.4.en: The names of the twelve sons of Ishmael are not mentioned elsewhere in the Holy Bible. Their mention indicates God's fulfilling of His promise to Abraham in answer to his prayer for Ishmael. For He said to him: "And as for Ishmael, I have heard thee: Behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiply him exceedingly; twelve princes shall he beget, and I will make him a great nation" (Gen 17:20).

1.66.5.en: Nebaioth: to him one of the Arab tribes is attributed (Gen 25:13, 16; 28:9; 36:3), described as having many flocks (Isa 60:7), and he was the brother of Mahalath and Basemath, whom Esau married.

1.66.6.en: Kedar: a Semitic name meaning "powerful or black," the father of the most famous Arab tribes, and their land is also called Kedar (Isa 21:16; Jer 49:28). They were for the most part nomadic shepherds living in black tents, and they are the Bedouin (Song 1:5). However, some of them were settled, dwelling in cities and towns (Isa 42:11). They are owners of many flocks, skilled in war, especially in shooting with the bow.

1.66.7.en: Adbeel: a Hebrew name meaning "discipline of God." He was perhaps the first father of the Arab tribe of Idibaʼilu. They lived in the northwest of the Arabian desert in the eighth century B.C., dwelling in the southwest of the Dead Sea. They are mentioned in the annals of Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria (Gen 12:1)(***).

1.66.8.en: Mibsam: a Hebrew name meaning "sweet fragrance."

1.67.0.en: Mishma, and Dumah, Massa, Hadad, and Tema, [30]

1.67.1.en: Mishma (Gen 25:14): a Hebrew name meaning "report." He was the son of Ishmael, perhaps the ancestor of the tribe of Banu Masmaʼ, who perhaps dwelt in Mount Masmaʼ, which lies between al-Jawf and Damascus.

1.67.3.en: Massa (Gen 25:14): his descendants are probably the Masani, whom Ptolemy placed in eastern Arabia near the borders of Babylon[59].

1.67.4.en: Hadad [Hadar (Gen 25:15)]: a Hebrew name meaning "sharpness and fierceness."

1.67.5.en: Tema [Tema (Gen 25:15)]: a Hebrew name, its meaning was "the southerner"; it was an Ishmaelite tribe descended from Tema, which dwelt in the land of the Arabs, in a region called Tema.

1.68.0.en: Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These are the sons of Ishmael. [31]

1.68.1.en: Jetur (Gen 25:15): his descendants dwelt in Iturea. The tribe of Jetur fought against the tribes of the children of Israel east of the Jordan.

1.68.2.en: Naphish (Gen 25:15): the tribe that includes his descendants, which dwelt east of the Jordan.

1.68.3.en: Kedemah or Qedemah (Gen 25:15): a Hebrew name meaning "eastern"; he dwelt east of the Jordan (Gen 25:18).

1.69.0.en: 32 Now the sons of Keturah, Abraham's concubine: she bare Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah. And the sons of Jokshan; Sheba, and Dedan. 33 And the sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher, and Henoch, and Abida, and Eldaah. All these are the sons of Keturah.

1.69.1.en: Now the sons of Keturah, Abraham's concubine: she bare

1.69.2.en: Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.

1.69.3.en: And the sons of Jokshan; Sheba, and Dedan. [32]

1.69.4.en: Keturah: a Hebrew name meaning incense; she bore six sons, who are the fathers of six Arab tribes. The Arab historians mention the tribe of Qatur, which dwells near Mecca. Origen sees that the word Keturah means incense or sweet fragrance.

1.69.5.en: v (Abraham) used to say like Paul: "For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ" (2 Cor 2:15).

1.69.6.en: Let us see how a person becomes the sweet fragrance of Christ.

1.69.7.en: Sin is a corrupt (foul) thing. In truth sinners are compared to swine who wallow in sins as in a foul mire. And David, as a repentant sinner, says: [My sores have festered and are afflicted] (cf. Ps 38:5) LXX; this is the man who marries Keturah[60].

1.69.8.en: Origen Origen sees that Abraham took Keturah as his wife when he was 137 years old, since Sarah died at the age of 127, and he was ten years older than she (Gen 25:1-2). He comments on this, saying:

1.69.9.en: [What then? Are we to suppose that the impulses of the flesh were revived in so great a Patriarch at this time?

1.69.10.en: And is the one of whom it is said that he had long since died to the natural instincts to be reckoned as having revived them in himself with lusts?

1.69.11.en: Or, as we have often said before, the marriages of the Patriarchs point to holy, mystical matters, as the one who said concerning wisdom supposes: "Therefore I purposed to take her to me to live with me" (Wis 8:9). Perhaps Abraham at that time was thinking of such a thing. For although he was wise, he knew that wisdom has no end, and that old age sets no limits to learning... The divine language calls learning his wife[61].]

1.69.12.en: Zimran (Gen 25:2): a Semitic name, perhaps meaning "wild cattle." Some think that his descendants dwell in Zabram, a city west of Qalla near the Red Sea, and others think they were the tribe of the Zamri in the middle of the land of the Arabs.

1.69.13.en: Jokshan (Gen 25:1-3): the son of Abraham by Keturah, and from him came Sheba and Dedan.

1.69.14.en: Medan (Gen 25:2): one of the sons of Abraham by Keturah, who perhaps dwelt in the valley of Medan near Dedan.

1.69.15.en: Ishbak: some think it means lean, and others that it means he surpasses. From his descendants came a tribe in northern Arabia[62].

1.69.16.en: Shuah (Gen 25:2): a Semitic name meaning "low." He was the son of Abraham by Keturah his wife. From him came an Arab tribe, from which came Bildad the Shuhite, and it was for the most part near the land of Uz (Job 2:11).

1.69.17.en: And the sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher, and Henoch, and Abida, and Eldaah.

1.70.0.en: All these are the sons of Keturah. [33]

1.70.1.en: We have not much to say about Midian the son of Abraham by Keturah. His descendants are reckoned among the children of the East, and perhaps Job was one of them, and they were separated from Isaac the son of the promise (Gen 25:6); they are mentioned only in this place.

1.70.2.en: Ephah: a Hebrew name meaning "darkness." Three bear this name, one of them the son of Midian the son of Abraham and his descendants after him, until the name became mixed between the man and the tribe (Gen 25:4), which dwelt in the northern regions of the Arabian peninsula.

1.70.3.en: Epher or Ephar (Gen 25:4): a Hebrew name meaning "young gazelle," the son of Midian.

1.70.4.en: Henoch (Gen 25:4): a Hebrew name meaning "student, trained; consecrated," the son of Midian, and of the descendants of Abraham by Keturah.

1.70.5.en: Abida: its meaning is "father of knowledge" or "my father knows," the fourth son of Abraham by his concubine Keturah. Abraham distributed gifts to his sons by the concubines and sent them away, so that they would not share the inheritance with Isaac.

1.70.6.en: Eldaah (Gen 25:4): a Hebrew name meaning "God has called," the son of Midian.

1.70.7.en: St. Augustine comments on Abraham's conduct toward the sons of the concubines such as the sons of Keturah, distinguishing between Isaac his son and them, encouraging us to realize the truth of our inheritance as free sons of God.

1.70.8.en: v Therefore, if we are the sons of the free Jerusalem, let us recognize that some of the gifts given to those who do not inherit differ from those given to the heirs. For it was said to the heirs: "For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father" (Rom 8:15)[63].

1.71.0.en: 34 And Abraham begat Isaac. The sons of Isaac; Esau and Israel. 35 The sons of Esau; Eliphaz, Reuel, and Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah. 36 The sons of Eliphaz; Teman, and Omar, Zephi, and Gatam, Kenaz, and Timna, and Amalek. 37 The sons of Reuel; Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.

1.71.2.en: The sons of Isaac; Esau and Israel. [34]

1.71.3.en: He did not mention here the name Jacob, but mentioned the name by which he was presented as a divine gift, "Israel," because from his sons He raised up the heads of the tribes of the people of God.

1.71.4.en: "Israel" is the name that was given to Jacob, and his descendants became the nation of the children of Israel, just as the descendants of Esau became the nation of Edom, which was in constant enmity with the children of Israel (Gen 21-36; 46-49).

1.71.5.en: Esau: it was not because of the dish of lentils in itself that Esau fell (Gen 25), but because of his recklessness.

1.71.6.en: v To make us know that the fault lies not in God's creation but in stubborn disobedience and excessive desire, the first man did not find death in the flesh of swine but in an apple (a fruit, since the Scripture does not say it was an apple) (Gen 3:6); and not because of a meal of birds, but for a dish of lentils Esau lost his birthright[64].

1.72.0.en: The sons of Esau; Eliphaz, Reuel, and Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah. [35]

1.72.1.en: The descendants of Edom (Esau) the son of Isaac bore a fierce enmity against Israel. Some of the families of Edom and their famous men are mentioned [35 ff.].

1.72.2.en: Eliphaz: its meaning in Hebrew is "God is refined gold."

1.73.0.en: The sons of Eliphaz; Teman, and Omar, Zephi, and Gatam, Kenaz, and Timna, and Amalek. [36]

1.73.1.en: Teman (Gen 36:11): a Hebrew name meaning "the right-hand" or "the southern," the firstborn of Eliphaz. It is the name of a tribe that took its name from him, located in the northern part of Edom, and called the land of the sons of the East, and it is called Teman (Ezek 25:13). Its people were famous for wisdom (Jer 49:17; Obad 9).

1.73.2.en: Omar: a name most probably derived from the Hebrew word "amar," meaning "he spoke." He is called a duke or chief in (Gen 36:15).

1.73.3.en: Zephi or Zepho (Gen 36:11, 15): Zepho is a Hebrew name meaning "watch," and he founded a tribe.

1.73.4.en: Gatam (Gen 36:11): a Hebrew name meaning "weak," a grandson of Esau and one of the dukes of Edom. It appears that a dukedom was named after him (Gen 36:16).

1.73.5.en: Kenaz: a Semitic name, perhaps meaning "hunting."

1.73.6.en: Timna: a Hebrew name meaning "restraint." It is the name of a duke of the dukes of Edom [36, 51]. Also one of the daughters of Seir, who was also Lotan's sister, who became a concubine to Eliphaz the son of Esau.

1.73.7.en: Amalek: if the descendants of Esau were called "Edom," who entered into constant resistance and enmity with Israel, then Amalek, the grandson of Esau, the ancestor of the tribe of the Amalekites, was the son of his father by his concubine (Gen 35:12). His people were known for their huge bodies together with violence and fierceness.

1.73.8.en: They lived in the desert region around the Dead Sea, plundering the cattle of other tribes as their booty. They were the first to attack Israel after their exodus from Egypt on their way to the Promised Land under the leadership of the prophet Moses (Ex 17:8). Amalek did not expect to be defeated before Israel, who had no military experience at that time.

1.74.0.en: The sons of Reuel; Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. [37]

1.74.1.en: Nahath: a Hebrew name meaning "rest." Three men are found who bear this name, and they are: 1. A grandson of Esau and Basemath and son of Reuel, who was a duke in the land of Edom (Gen 36:13). 2. A Levite of the sons of the Kohathites, son of Zophai and an ancestor of the prophet Samuel (1 Chr 6:26). 3. A Levite whom King Hezekiah appointed as one of the overseers of the offerings of the Temple under the supervision of Cononiah the Levite and Shimei his brother (2 Chr 31:13).

1.75.0.en: 38 And the sons of Seir; Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah, and Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan. 39 And the sons of Lotan; Hori, and Homam: and Timna was Lotan's sister. 40 The sons of Shobal; Alian, and Manahath, and Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. And the sons of Zibeon; Aiah, and Anah. 41 The sons of Anah; Dishon. And the sons of Dishon; Amram, and Eshban, and Ithran, and Cheran. 42 The sons of Ezer; Bilhan, and Zavan, and Jakan. The sons of Dishan; Uz, and Aran.

1.75.1.en: And the sons of Seir; Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah, and Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan. [38]

1.75.2.en: Lotan (Gen 36:20): an Edomite name, perhaps a form of Lot, ending with nunation. It was applied to a tribe of the Horites, who dwell in Mount Seir and are ruled by a chief.

1.75.3.en: Shobal (Gen 36:20): it is probable that he was a sheikh of the Horites.

1.75.4.en: Zibeon (Gen 36:20): a Hivite or Horite name meaning "hyena," a Horite prince. Perhaps he migrated with his family to Mount Seir, and the tribe of the Horites came from him.

1.75.5.en: Anah (Gen 36:24): a Semitic name, perhaps meaning "listening." Among those who bore this name was a Horite chief [38], and another, the son of Zibeon, who found the wild doves [40].

1.75.6.en: Dishon (Gen 36:21): a Semitic name meaning "gazelle." The name of one of the sons of Seir the Horite.

1.75.7.en: Ezer: its meaning in Hebrew is "help or aid," and he was a duke of the sons of Seir the Horite in Edom.

1.75.8.en: Dishan (Gen 36:21): a Semitic name meaning "gazelle." The name of one of the sons of Seir the Horite.

1.76.0.en: And the sons of Lotan; Hori, and Homam: and Timna was Lotan's sister. [39]

1.76.1.en: Hori (Gen 36:22, 30): it is probable that it is an Egyptian name taken from the name of the god Horus. Many bear this name. This name is also applied to an individual of the clan of Hur of the sons of Gad (1 Chr 5:14). Seir is also given the title "Hori" (Gen 36:20).

1.76.2.en: Homam or Heman (Gen 36:22): an Edomite name meaning "confusion or tumult."

1.76.3.en: Timna (Gen 36:40): a Hebrew name meaning "restraint." The daughter of Seir and sister of Lotan, who became a concubine to Eliphaz the son of Esau and the mother of Amalek. There is another, who was a duke of the dukes of Edom.

1.77.0.en: The sons of Shobal; Alian, and Manahath, and Ebal, Shephi, and Onam.

1.77.1.en: And the sons of Zibeon; Aiah, and Anah. [40]

1.77.2.en: Alian or Alvan (Gen 36:23): its meaning is "high," of the descendants of Seir the Horite.

1.77.3.en: Manahath (Gen 36:23): a Hebrew name meaning "rest," the name of a person of the descendants of Seir the Horite.

1.77.4.en: Ebal (Gen 36:23), of the descendants of Seir the Horite. There is also another person who bears the same name (1 Chr 1:22), and he was called Obal (Gen 10:28).

1.77.5.en: Shephi or Shepho (Gen 36:23): a Hebrew name meaning "bare." He was of the sons of Shobal, of the sons of Seir the Horite.

1.77.6.en: Onam: its meaning in Hebrew is "strong."

1.77.7.en: Aiah: a Hebrew name meaning "falcon." The brother of Anah, the father of one of the wives of Esau the son of Isaac (Gen 36:24).

1.78.0.en: The sons of Anah; Dishon. And the sons of Dishon; Amram, and Eshban, and Ithran, and Cheran. [41]

1.78.1.en: Amram: a Hebrew name meaning "red," of the sons of Seir, and also called Hemdan, a Hebrew name meaning "pleasant" or "delightful, desirable."

1.78.2.en: Eshban: perhaps its meaning is "thinker or intelligent," the name of one of the sons of Dishon the Horite, one of the chiefs of Mount Seir (Gen 36:26).

1.78.3.en: Ithran (Gen 36:26): a Hebrew name meaning "excellence," a Horite prince.

1.78.4.en: Cheran: a Semitic name, perhaps meaning "like a lamb," a Horite (Gen 36:26).

1.79.0.en: The sons of Ezer; Bilhan, and Zavan, and Jakan.

1.79.1.en: The sons of Dishan; Uz, and Aran. [42]

1.79.2.en: Zavan (Gen 36:27): a Hebrew name meaning "disturbed and restless." The son of Ezer, a Horite prince.

1.79.3.en: Jakan (Num 33:31-32): at the time of the Exodus the sons of Jakan formed a tribe that occupied a region on the border of Edom near Mount Hor where Aaron died, and the children of Israel took some of their wells (Deut 10:6; Num 33:31-32).

1.79.4.en: Uz (Gen 10:23): to him is attributed the tribe of the Arameans, and the tribe was also attributed to Nahor (Gen 22:21) and to Dishan the Horite (Gen 36:28). Job dwelt in the land of Uz (Job 1:1).

1.79.5.en: Aran: its meaning is "young wild goat" (Gen 36), and perhaps he is Oren the Jerahmeelite (1 Chr 2:25); the name is of the kind of naming a person or family after an animal, as was the custom among the Arabs, and still is in Syria, such as the family of Lion or Tiger or Gazelle.

1.79.6.en: More than a third of the Horites, the descendants of Seir, bear the names of animals, and some of the Edomites also bear the names of animals. The name "Seir" itself means "kid," and the name Dishan means "gazelle."

1.80.0.en: 43 Now these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the children of Israel; Bela the son of Beor: and the name of his city was Dinhabah. 44 And when Bela was dead, Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his stead. 45 And when Jobab was dead, Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his stead. 46 And when Husham was dead, Hadad the son of Bedad, which smote Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Avith. 47 And when Hadad was dead, Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his stead. 48 And when Samlah was dead, Shaul of Rehoboth by the river reigned in his stead. 49 And when Shaul was dead, Baal-hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his stead. 50 And when Baal-hanan was dead, Hadad reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Pai; and his wife's name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab. 51 Hadad died also. And the dukes of Edom were; duke Timnah, duke Aliah, duke Jetheth, 52 Duke Aholibamah, duke Elah, duke Pinon, 53 Duke Kenaz, duke Teman, duke Mibzar, 54 Duke Magdiel, duke Iram. These are the dukes of Edom.

1.80.1.en: Now these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before any king reigned over the children of Israel; Bela the son of Beor:

1.80.2.en: and the name of his city was Dinhabah. [43]

1.80.3.en: The book recorded for us the descendants of Edom (Esau), who were enemies of the children of Israel. Esau was the eldest son of Isaac, of the offspring of Abraham the man of faith, but since he married pagan women, who represented bitterness in the life of Rebekah, the wife of Isaac and the mother of Esau and Jacob, the Edomite nation arose, hostile to the divine truth, worshipping idols.

1.80.4.en: Bela the son of Beor (Gen 36:32): a Hebrew name meaning "swallowing or ruin," he was a king over Edom.

1.80.5.en: Dinhabah (Gen 36:32): an Edomite name, perhaps meaning "he who gives judgment." It was the capital of Bela king of Edom. Perhaps its site today is "Khirbet ed-Dan," a town in Moab a little south of the Arnon.

1.81.0.en: And when Bela was dead, Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his stead. [44]

1.81.1.en: Jobab (Gen 36:33): a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "a cry." He was the son of Joktan [23], and it is not known where this Arab tribe dwelt. One of the kings of Moab also bears the same name (Gen 36:23-34; 1 Chr 1:44-45).

1.82.0.en: And when Jobab was dead, Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his stead. [45]

1.82.1.en: Husham (Gen 36:34): a Hebrew name meaning "haste" and "emotion." A man from the land of the Temanites, who succeeded Jobab as king over Edom.

1.83.0.en: Hadad the son of Bedad, which smote Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Avith. [46]

1.83.1.en: Hadad or Hadar (Gen 36:35-36): a Semitic name meaning "brave," a king of Edom; his father's name was Bedad, and his capital was Avith. There is another Edomite king with the same name (Gen 36:39), whose capital was Pau or Pai.

1.83.2.en: Avith (Gen 36:35): an Edomite name meaning "ruin," an Edomite city, the birthplace of King Hadad. Perhaps it is today "Mahal el-Juthth" near Maan.

1.84.0.en: And when Hadad was dead, Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his stead. [47]

1.84.1.en: Samlah (Gen 36:36): a Hebrew name meaning "garment." The name of one of the ancient kings of Edom. He reigned before there was a king in Israel, and the capital of his kingdom was Masrekah.

1.84.2.en: Masrekah (Gen 36:36): an Edomite name, perhaps meaning "vineyard," a city in Edom, the birthplace of Samlah king of Edom, which is on Mount Mishraq, which lies twenty-two miles south of Maan.

1.85.0.en: And when Samlah was dead, Shaul of Rehoboth by the river reigned in his stead. [48]

1.85.1.en: Shaul of Rehoboth (Gen 36:37): Shaul is a Hebrew name meaning "asked of God." He was one of the kings of Edom, from Rehoboth, which lies on the River Euphrates (Gen 36:37).

1.86.0.en: And when Shaul was dead, Baal-hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his stead. [49]

1.86.1.en: Achbor (Gen 36:38): Achbor is a Semitic name meaning "mouse"; he was a king of Edom.

1.87.0.en: And when Baal-hanan was dead, Hadad reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Pai; and his wife's name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab. [50]

1.87.1.en: Mehetabel the daughter of Matred (Gen 36:39): a Semitic name meaning "one to whom God is kind." The daughter of Matred and wife of Hadad king of Edom.

1.88.0.en: Hadad died also. And the dukes of Edom were;

1.88.1.en: duke Timnah, duke Aliah, duke Jetheth, [51]

1.89.0.en: Duke Aholibamah, duke Elah, duke Pinon, [52]

1.89.1.en: Aholibamah (Gen 36:41): a Hebrew name meaning "my tent is a high place," a duke in Edom.

1.89.2.en: The wife of Esau bore the same name, the daughter of Anah the Hivite (Gen 36:2), and she was also called Judith.

1.89.3.en: Elah (or Elath): a Hebrew name meaning "oak tree," a duke in Edom (Gen 36:41).

1.89.4.en: Pinon (Gen 36:41): a duke in Edom, who perhaps dwelt in the city of Punon, lying on the eastern side of the Arabah about five and a half miles east of Khirbet Nahas.

1.90.0.en: Duke Kenaz, duke Teman, duke Mibzar, [53]

1.90.1.en: Kenaz (Gen 36:42): a Semitic name, perhaps meaning "hunting." He was the son of Eliphaz the son of Esau (Gen 36:11), and became a duke in Edom.

1.90.2.en: Teman (Gen 36:42): a Hebrew name meaning "the right-hand or the southern," the firstborn of Eliphaz the son of Esau, who became a duke in Edom.

1.90.3.en: Mibzar (Gen 36:42): a Hebrew name meaning "fortress," a duke in Edom.

1.91.1.en: These are the dukes of Edom. [54]

1.91.2.en: Magdiel (Gen 36:43): an Edomite name meaning "glory of God," a duke in Edom.

1.91.3.en: Iram (Gen 36:43): a Hebrew name meaning "watchful," a duke in Edom.

1.91.4.en: A genealogy, or a journey with God?!

1.91.5.en: v By Your Holy Spirit open my eyes, that I may enjoy the sweetness of the joyful journey of life with You!

1.91.6.en: I stand in perplexity, with wondrous amazement at the works of Your love!

1.91.7.en: I see in the genealogy (1 Chr 1-9) a delightful journey in Your company.

1.91.8.en: I will not begin it unless I throw myself into Your embrace and feel Your company with me.

1.91.9.en: I see that You are the beginning of the journey and You are its end, and You are the One who carries my depths, so I rest upon Your shoulders all along the way!

1.91.10.en: v The Jews cared to record the genealogies, that every believer might know to which tribe he belongs!

1.91.11.en: And might know his portion of the Promised Land in Canaan!

1.91.12.en: But as for me, I reckon myself as though I belong to the tribe of the heavenly ones!

1.91.13.en: I look for nothing but the heavenly Canaan, my eternal inheritance!

1.91.14.en: You are my portion, my wealth, my treasure, my joy and my crown.

1.91.15.en: Grant me to meet some of my fathers, and to enter with them into a frank conversation of love, that I may enjoy the journey of my life.

1.91.16.en: I meet Adam, and see him rejoicing and happy!

1.91.17.en: I hear him say: "Since my God gave me Seth as a son, I was comforted.

1.91.18.en: I saw him bearing my image as I was before the corruption, to some degree.

1.91.19.en: I saw him as a type of the new Adam, my Savior and the Savior of my offspring.

1.91.20.en: I was comforted together with the partner of my life, and we no longer remembered Cain, the killer of his brother.

1.91.21.en: I no longer saw him trembling and terrified, as though all creation were against him.

1.91.22.en: I no longer grieved over Abel, whose blood cries to heaven!

1.91.23.en: I saw You, my Savior, and I rejoiced because my offspring clung to You.

1.91.24.en: By Your blood, O Lover of mankind, You repaired what I had corrupted in the life of all my offspring!

1.91.25.en: v I went on from Adam and Eve to their grandson Enosh!

1.91.26.en: I rejoiced when I saw him, and understood what the prophet Moses wrote about him:

1.91.27.en: Then began men to call upon the name of the LORD" (Gen 4:26).

1.91.28.en: I saw him distinguished, for he was the first to praise God without ceasing.

1.91.29.en: His heart was aflame with love for You, so he praised You by day and by night.

1.91.30.en: He became the first teacher of the life of praise!

1.91.31.en: He longed that all the offspring of Adam would share with the heavenly ones their praises.

1.91.32.en: v The personality of his grandson Mahalaleel drew me; his life is in harmony with his name, he does not cease to rejoice in You.

1.91.33.en: His heart, which knows nothing but thanksgiving and praise to God, presented to us from his offspring "Enoch," who was found worthy to be translated by the Lord to Himself.

1.91.34.en: Let me repeat with the wise man: "He was snatched away lest evil should change his mind...

1.91.35.en: He was living among sinners and He translated him" (Wis 4:10-11).

1.91.36.en: Enoch flew on the wings of love, when he was caught up to heaven (Gen 5:24).

1.91.37.en: v Enoch passed quickly through the days of his exile, and the Lord gathered him to Himself from the face of evil.

1.91.38.en: And his son Methuselah came and lived nearly a thousand years.

1.91.39.en: His life was very long, but his life ended in death.

1.91.40.en: The years of his life passed like a moment of time, so it no longer concerns us how many years we dwell in exile.

1.91.41.en: v His son Lamech opened a dangerous door in the life of mankind.

1.91.42.en: He was not committed, like the first man, to one Eve.

1.91.43.en: Lamech was the first to marry two women, and so he corrupted the concept of marital love and the unity of the family.

1.91.44.en: We say with St. Mar Ephrem that by his marriage his life was filled with toil.

1.91.45.en: So he looked forward to the Messiah born of a virgin to give him rest and righteousness.

1.91.46.en: v I pass quickly to righteous Noah in the midst of a dark and crooked generation.

1.91.47.en: The Lord commanded him to make an ark, in order to flood the whole world.

1.91.48.en: And Noah and his three sons with their wives begin a new world.

1.91.49.en: It is as though Noah and his family were baptized in the midst of the Flood.

1.91.50.en: The ark preserved them, as though they enjoyed the type of the Church of the New Testament.

1.91.51.en: The outer world was renewed, that our inner depths may be constantly renewed.

1.91.52.en: v As for the three sons of Noah, when Noah was uncovered, wicked Ham mocked him.

1.91.53.en: While Shem and Japheth, in dignity, covered him.

1.91.54.en: I saw Your image, O You whom Your love for us made drunk, so You were stripped on the Cross to bear our shame.

1.91.55.en: The Jews who crucified You mocked You.

1.91.56.en: And the nations and peoples believed in You, and became members of Your holy body.

1.91.57.en: v I met the father of the believers, Abraham.

1.91.58.en: I rejoiced when I met him, for Adam is the common father of all mankind, and Abraham is the common father of the believers.
